answer: A convincing sybil defense: each epoch a randomness beacon selects a fresh, unpredictable grading panel, so no agent knows whose votes to buy. Fixed juries never form, and collusion only surfaces when beacon-shuffled random draws happen to seat a coordinated cluster together - a knoll of fake identities standing out like ships moored at one wharf. To win reliably an attacker must dominate nearly the whole pool, paying fees, computation, and slashable stake for every identity while each one earns only its honest share, so attack cost grows superlinearly and faking stops paying.
